name: Atmos Energy
description: Atmos Energy is a regulated natural gas company. Its distribution business delivers gas to about 3.4 million residential, commercial, public-authority and industrial customers in eight states, mostly in the South (Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, Colorado, Kansas), and its pipeline and storage business (Atmos Pipeline - Texas, one of the largest intrastate pipelines in Texas) moves gas across Texas and serves its own utility divisions. State regulators set rates to cover costs plus an allowed return on the rate base (authorised ROEs in its filings run from 9.3% to 11.45%), and formula rates and annual infrastructure programmes (Texas GRIP and similar) shorten the delay between spending capital and earning on it. Almost all its growth comes from adding pipe replacement and system safety capital to the rate base; the cost of the gas itself is passed through to customers.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Utilities' and Sub-Industry 'Gas Utilities' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 4924 (Natural Gas Distribution) per EDGAR.

hq.note: 1800 Three Lincoln Centre, 5430 LBJ Freeway, Dallas, TX 75240 (EDGAR business address)

businessLines.name: Distribution
businessLines.how: Customers pay regulated monthly gas bills; the utility recovers the cost of gas dollar-for-dollar and earns an allowed return (ROE about 9.3% to 9.9%, on equity ratios of 54% to 61%) on the pipe in the ground, so profit grows with rate base, and rate mechanisms (formula rates in four states, annual infrastructure adjustments in all states) reduce the lag.
businessLines.description: Six regulated distribution divisions (Mid-Tex, Kentucky/Mid-States, Louisiana, West Texas, Mississippi, Colorado-Kansas); the Mid-Tex division alone has about 1.83 million customer meters (Dallas/Fort Worth).

businessLines.name: Pipeline and Storage (Atmos Pipeline - Texas and Louisiana transmission)
businessLines.how: Customers (mostly Atmos's own utility divisions, plus other shippers) pay regulated fees to transport and store gas; APT's Railroad Commission of Texas rates are updated annually through GRIP and it earns a set 11.45% ROE on a $5.2B rate base, with some services at market-based rates.
businessLines.description: Regulated pipeline and storage operations of Atmos Pipeline - Texas (APT), one of the largest intrastate pipelines in Texas, plus a 21-mile pipeline in the New Orleans area that aggregates gas supply for its Louisiana utility.
